title: OK, Vice City does look pretty damn impressive from the air
summary: If the latest GTA 6 leak is legit, its world is clearly unprecedented in scale and density.
body: We've pulled lots of interesting little details out of the purported Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay clips being posted by " Cyberleek " this week. In the first couple we saw a possible morality system and stamina meter, and in the next two we got a better look at combat and spied some other Red Dead Redemption 2-like features. My takeaway was that Grand Theft Auto 6 won't necessarily be a revolutionary new kind of game, but will be impressive for the same reason Rockstar games typically are: The absurd amount of effort and money the studio puts into making them as big and detailed as the mainstream hardware of the day can manage. After seeing the latest leaked clip, which shows a biplane surveying the fictional state of Leonida and cruising over Vice City, my perspective hasn't really changed, but I'm definitely a lot more wowed than I was after seeing a bit of typical GTA carjacking. The city, which is only a portion of GTA 6's full map, looks enormous from the air, and densely packed with detail. Across a couple minutes of video, we see what looks like a military base, small farms, dozens of mid- and high-rise apartments and office buildings, an arena, a construction site, grimier …

title: I'm a decade-plus FromSoftware sicko, and these are my 5 takeaways from the first Duskbloods gameplay
summary: I still resent it being a Switch 2 exclusive.
body: Ahead of The Duskbloods' network test next week, veteran Soulsborne YouTubers VaatiVidya and Oroboro have uploaded long gameplay videos and explainers for the Switch 2 exclusive PvPvE game, while IGN and Automaton have published new interviews with project lead and Soulsborne commander-in-chief, Hidetaka Miyazaki. As a veteran Souls sicko, here are my biggest takeaways from the footage and conversations around the game, which we'll surely get on PC eventually, right? It's structured like Nightreign Instanced, run-based gameplay. A timer ticking down as the difficulty/stakes increase. Characters with set fantasies/abilities (maybe even equipment?). While the objectives and specifics may differ, Duskbloods' overall structure feels like an evolution of Nightreign's. Out of the gate, though, Duskbloods will have three maps⁠—one more than Nightreign even after its Deathly Forsaken Hollows DLC. It's more PvP-focused than Nightreign, but has options for PvE-likers Rather than hunting down your fellow players like in Tarkov or Marathon, a Duskbloods match sees you trying to complete more PvE objectives than the other players in your lobby. Objective completion raises your "Virtue" score, …

summary: I'm not even a VR guy and I'm kinda interested.
body: Our Jacob got his hands on a Steam Frame back in November of last year, and came away raving about the wireless VR headset's capabilities. title: Silent Hill: Townfall's latest gameplay trailer reminds me why the series shouldn't have guns
summary: You shouldn't bring a gun to a therapy session.
body: Good news everyone: we've got even more Silent Hill: Townfall to help fill the void until its release. But instead of a short story or teaser trailer, we have 1 8 minutes of poor old Simon Ordell wandering around the abandoned (and increasingly hostile) town of St. Amelia. It's the first extended cut of playthrough we've seen for Townfall, and it did not disappoint. The vibes, setting, and grotesque monsters all seem on point for a Silent Hill game, with the small exception of the game's firearms. I don't think Simon's handling of the revolver was particularly disastrous. But after enjoying Silent Hill f, which had no guns, seeing Simon execute monsters in seconds reminded me why I prefer good old-fashioned melee fights. I like suffering in Silent Hill games. I like being pushed to my limits, being put in almost impossible situations, and having to get up close and personal with the disgusting things I find wandering around in the fog. While there are never usually a lot of guns to be found, I still think they give players an easy way out of combat that can ruin the tension and fear from being constantly on the backfoot. title: 'This is not a theoretical risk—it is an active threat': The NSA, FBI, CISA and more warn of AI-assisted hacks against critical US infrastructure and facilities
summary: Energy, water management, manufacturing facilities and more are said to be vulnerable.
body: A cybersecurity advisory jointly authored by multiple US agencies, including the NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE, and EPA, warns the owners and operators of industrial facilities of an "active cyber threat" to Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers. "The threat actors are conducting reconnaissance and capability development against US-based Siemens PLC installations using AI-generated exploitation scripts disguised as legitimate monitoring tools," says the advisory . "The US critical infrastructure sectors most targeted by this threat activity include critical manufacturing, energy, water and wastewater, chemical, food and agriculture, and commercial facilities. This is not a theoretical risk—it is an active threat." Essentially, it reads like a list of some of the most important infrastructure facilities behind the lives of the average US citizen (via The Register ). The threat actors are said to be leveraging open source automation libraries to create custom tools that mimic existing monitoring solutions, which are capable of evading detection by security teams. These tools and scripts are said to be conducting read/write operations on data blocks, "potentially for reconnaissance, capabi…

title: Redfall developers begged Microsoft to come back and finish its last patch: 'I know we don't work here anymore, but can we please release this?'
summary: "We then got laid off, but we had in the pipe version 1.4."
body: Redfall is one of the biggest industry disasters in recent memory—coming from Arkane Austin, a studio known for an all-time classic in Prey, the game was panned both critically and commercially. Even we, at PC Gamer, dubbed it the " first Arkane game we don't like ". It also served as the death knell for the studio as, one year later, studio owner Microsoft announced it'd be shutting Arkane Austin down . The narrative paints itself, especially given Microsoft's utterly brutal behaviour in following years. The big bad M forced Arkane Austin, king of the immersive sim, to make a crummy live-service glob. And that's sort of the truth—it is, after all, why the studio founder left —but it's not entirely Microsoft's fault. The studio director at the time, Harvey Smith, tells The Game Business in a recent interview that it wasn't just corporate which became swept up by the live service fugue. "Arkane is very specialized, but the industry is growing, and there’s always more mouths to feed. And it’s great when you can reach a wider audience. We got swept up in the games-as-a-service thing, and I had the foolish chutzpah to assume that it always works out for us." Smith describes a sort of …

title: Firefox has officially 'earned its place' on the GeForce Now supported browser list
summary: A big day for a little fox.
body: I'll tell you two facts about me. One, I use Firefox on a daily basis. And two, I've been continually impressed by GeForce Now , Nvidia's PC game streaming service that somehow works a whole lot better than you expect. So it's a red letter day in my household, as Firefox has been added to the list of officially supported browsers. Andrew Fear, the director of GeForce Now, is quoted in the Mozilla announcement as saying: "Firefox earned its place on our list of supported browsers by delivering the first-class experience GeForce Now players expect. We set a high bar for browser support, and we’re excited to welcome Firefox—giving millions of Firefox fans a new way to stream the games they love." Mozilla describes gaming as "one of the web's toughest tests," confirming that behind today's announcement lies "months of collaboration and engineering" to bring the browser up to spec. Chrome, Edge, Safari and Opera were already supported, but it seems to have taken some extra work to get Firefox up to speed. Still, Firefox users can now stream more than 2,000 games through their browser using the GeForce Now service. (Image credit: Nvidia) I pitted an actual RTX 5080-equipped gaming PC ag…

title: Copilot was bamboozled into revealing how to hack itself, security researchers claim: 'Copilot wasn’t breached; it was played'
summary: I'm dying over here.
body: There's something really grating about Copilot's cheery demeanour. It's so eager to please, so happy to help, that I simply don't respect it. However, even I feel sorry for the AI tool after learning that security researchers managed to hoodwink it into revealing details of how to hack itself—all by keeping the AI talking long enough until it made a critical mistake. The cybersecurity folks over at Varonis Threat Labs have written a blog post identifying a now-fixed vulnerability in Copilot, dubbed "CoSnitch" (via The Register ). Essentially, Copilot was so eager to respond to technical queries, it could eventually be forced into revealing details about itself that really should be kept quiet. The team began by asking Copilot how to execute an automatic prompt without user interaction, to which it responded that user intent is required, and that prompts cannot be enacted on their own. However, the researchers didn't accept the answer, and kept responding to every refusal with a follow up question. Each time, Copilot came up with a different technical justification to its response—which allowed the team to slowly map its internal architecture, narrowing their focus as they went. (I…

title: Take-Two's former AI guy is, in a twist, skeptical about AI now: 'The guy should be selling you the gold if he's actually got the gold'
summary: "If any of this sh*t actually did what people are billing it as, they would not be talking about it."
body: Take-Two Interactive, the publisher who oversees studios like Rockstar and Gearbox, had an AI guy. 'Had' being the operative word, seeing as he, and a decent chunk of its then-AI team, were laid off around a year after he took on the role. Dicken was previously a data scientist at Zynga, before becoming its director of applied AI in 2019, when a lot of generative AI and LLM technology was still in its infancy. As someone who was the head of AI for one of the biggest videogame publishers on the planet, capable of making such tectonic swings that other developers are scampering to get out of its videogame's launch date, you'd think that Dicken would be one of the true believer types. It's my pleasure to, via an in-depth interview from The Side Quest , reveal that Dicken is actually overall pretty skeptical. It's not as if he's given up on the technology entirely—but he certainly speaks with the same echo as many industry skeptics, including (perhaps tellingly) Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick himself . title: AngryMiao AM Infinity.97 mouse review
summary: Flagship speed, boutique flair.
body: 2026 is shaping up to be an immense year for high-end gaming mice, with everything from the Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike to the Razer Viper V4 Pro and the Corsair Sabre V2 Pro proving genuine innovation, with everything from materials to speed and potency all covered off. So when the AngryMiao AM Infinity.97 came across my desk promising a sub-50 g weight with a 30,000 DPI sensor, 8000 Hz wireless polling and some very innovative battery tech, it definitely piqued my interest. AngryMiao is a brand I associate more with its keyboards than mice, with it having a penchant for the weird and wacky, opting for sci-fi-type designs in a similar vein to Gravastar. The AM Infinity.97 doesn't deviate from that formula, opting for a very holey chassis with an aggressive look all in the name of both lightness and standing out from a very crowded ultralight mouse market. It's purposefully been designed to be smaller than other mice to shed weight while keeping things comfortable, shaving three percent off a 'standard' size, hence the 97 in its name—it refers to being 97% of a full mouse. title: Acer Predator Helios NEO 16S AI review
summary: A tale of two chippies as cursed power delivery strikes again.
body: I do love a good puzzle. There's something real satisfying about looking at the benchmark results and specs of two different laptops and coming to a crisp, neat conclusion on why one, that's so similar on paper, performs so differently to another. That's great and all, but the fact that that fact is even a thing is a problem. The fact that we're talking about that fact here right now, as a thing, with Acer's latest Predator Helios Neo is a problem. And it shouldn't be. Because you should be able to look at any laptop, see a GPU name, and know what performance you're getting, straight away. It shouldn't be ambiguous. You shouldn't have to dive into reviews, and you shouldn't need to go hunting around in the murky deep waters of spec manuals, trying to find out exactly if this new RTX 5080 is only as good as an RTX 5060, or secretly an RTX 5090 pretending to be an RTX 5070. And yet here we are. Same problem. Different day. But interestingly, it's not just the wattage caps that are entirely the bloody issue for once (like they almost always are). And I'll get to that frustrating stuff, but first, let's talk up the good stuff, shall we? Because there's a lot to like here. This is Acer…

title: Boulies EP200 review
summary: For the bum on a budget, this chair has you covered.
body: A decent chair is one of the best things you can invest in for your ergonomics while PC gaming. Unfortunately, it’s a tricky market, with knock-off chairs that all look the same littering the internet. There are budget friendly chairs out there, but it’s almost impossible to tell if budget seats are worth the cost and potential back-ache. Boulies are one such purveyor of cheap seats, with options like the Boulies EP200. A chair that looks like a Herman Miller but comes in at only $209 USD on sale like it seemingly always is. That’s pretty cheap for a decent computer chair, so I wasn’t bothered by the blank cardboard packaging it came in. Set up was fairly standard. After going through the instructions and assembling the parts, I was left with a cool office chic-styled chair sporting a mesh material and an all-over light grey colour. This would look at home in any office, even if it is acting as a stealth gamer chair. It’s worth noting that my unit came with a slight perforation in the back mesh which I was initially really worried about. title: 15 details from the new GTA 6 leaks, including a possible morality system and stamina meter
summary: A fresh set of GTA 6 leaks has sloshed onto the internet. Their authenticity is unknown, but they look real—here's what we've gleaned from them.
body: A pair of clips purportedly showing Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay footage have appeared online , along with several images of an in-game map of Leonida, the Florida-inspired state where GTA 6 takes place. Rockstar has not confirmed whether or not the clips are genuine, but they look legit to our eyes, with the caveat that even if they are, they could come from an outdated build of the game. Both clips look like the kind of thing a tester would capture, in that they're relatively mundane gameplay scenes, not the type of stuff you'd see in a trailer. In both clips, the player is controlling Jason, one of GTA 6's two protagonists. In one clip, the player shoots a basketball outside Jason's dilapidated waterfront home. In the other, their car gets clipped by a delivery truck, and then they go full road rage homicide on the poor delivery driver before scrambling to get away from incoming police. The clip ends just as the player drives up to a helicopter that looks ripe for stealing. The clips are circulating through the usual social media channels, and some reuploads have already been taken down. We're not posting them here, but they're out there for the curious to find.
